newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee ends slightly lower, awaits ACPC news.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee ends slightly lower, awaits ACPC news.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures settled modestly lower in thin dealings Friday, as the market continued to stall while traders awaited news from producers' talks in London.

The Association of Coffee Producing Countries' (ACPC) technical group met Friday to prepare for the full council meeting on Saturday, delegates said. While no major policy revisions are expected, dealers said uncertainty ahead of the talks has kept futures confined to a small range.
"We are waiting for the ACPC to finish meeting," one trader said. "Next week we won't have any reasons not to move because that factor is no longer going to be in the market."
Traders said that local participation accounted for the bulk of today's activity. Turnover was light, with an estimated 4,632 lots changing hands.
Benchmark December futures dipped 0.45 cent per lb, to end at 105.25, having traded from 106.20 to 104.70. Second-month March fell 1.10 to 101.40, while the rest lost 1.15 to 1.50.

After posting losses for the second day in a row, traders said December's technical stance was beginning to look a bit bearish. They said a break through the 102 level could lead to a test of the psychologically important 100-cent mark.
On the upside, one trader said the December contract would need to breach 108.00 to start a move up towards the 115-120 level.
